findings: E01 enumeration independently verified and correct. Slots S1/S2/S3; D1 (display, S1-S3), D2 (display, S2-S3); R1 allows only S1 so R1->(D1,S1) is forced (D2 unavailable at S1). Remaining options: R2 in {(D1,S2),(D2,S2)}, R3/R4 in {(D1,S2),(D1,S3),(D2,S2),(D2,S3)} each; counting pairwise (device,slot)-disjoint triples gives 6+6=12, matching baseline_count=12 (evidence.json:4) and baseline_expected_solution_count=12 (exercise-data.json:631). Under D2_closed only D1's 3 device-slots remain for 4 requests, so 0 solutions (evidence.json:5; exercise-data.json:632-633); the pigeonhole unsat_argument (4>3, then 3 requests competing for S2/S3 after R1 occupies S1) is sound. The reference assignment R1->D1/S1, R2->D1/S2, R3->D2/S2, R4->D1/S3 (exercise-data.json:609-630) satisfies all hard constraints (exercise-data.json:365-370) and is one of the 12.

E03 enumeration independently verified and correct. Q1 (10人, projector, S1 only) is forced to (C1,S1) since C2 is unavailable at S1; Q3 (20人) exceeds C1 capacity 12 so must use C2; Q4 needs computers so must use C2; Q3 and Q4 therefore occupy C2-S2 and C2-S3 in either order, and Q2 cannot use C2-S2 (that would strand Q3/Q4 on the single remaining C2 slot), so Q2 is forced to (C1,S2): exactly 2 feasible solutions, matching baseline_count=2 (evidence.json:68). The reference assignment (exercise-data.json:389-410) is feasible (Q2 8<=12, Q3 20<=24, Q4 16<=24, facilities subset satisfied). Variant C2_capacity18 leaves Q3 (20人) above both capacities 12 and 18, giving 0 solutions (evidence.json:69; exercise-data.json:423, 448-453). The per-request option sets in evidence.json:70-111 match my derivation (1, 3, 2, 2).

E05 enumeration independently verified and correct. P1 (general, S1) is forced to (V1,S1) since V2 is unavailable at S1; P3 (screen_reader) can only use V2. Counting distinct (resource,slot) assignments for (P2,P3,P4) gives 4+2=6, matching baseline_count=6 (evidence.json:128). Under V2_without_screen_reader no resource holds screen_reader for P3, giving 0 solutions (evidence.json:129; exercise-data.json:588, 660-667). The reference assignment P1->V1/S1, P2->V1/S2, P3->V2/S2, P4->V1/S3 (exercise-data.json:566-587) is feasible and among the 6. The option sets in evidence.json:130-178 match my derivation (1, 3, 2, 4).

E04 arithmetic verified and causal boundary respected. Baseline 4 lamps x 20W x 6h/day x 30 days = 14,400 Wh = 14.4 kWh; candidate A: 4 x 30W x 6 x 30 = 21.6 kWh (+50%); candidate B unchanged at 14.4 kWh — all match evidence.json:117-120 and the guidance checks (exercise-data.json:232-234); 1kWh=1000Wh conversion is stated (exercise-data.json:557). Stair hesitation rates 8/40=0.2 (N1) and 9/60=0.15 (N2) match evidence.json:121-124 and exercise-data.json:235-236, computed from observations O1/O2 (exercise-data.json:484-505). The causal boundary statements (evidence.json:125; exercise-data.json:293) are consistent with the confounded observational design — N1 vs N2 differ in weather, umbrella use and event context, not only illuminance (8 vs 12 lx) — and with the disclosed known_evidence_gaps (exercise-data.json:558-563). Both candidate costs (A 3600, B 2800) are within the stated 4000元 one-time cap. No misleading causal claim found in the materials.

Concern: the packaged machine evidence is an empty file. input_sha256 lists executable-evidence.json as e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 (evidence.json:197), which is the well-known SHA-256 of the empty string. So although a verification_script_sha256 is recorded (evidence.json:199), no non-empty enumeration output artifact accompanies it; the reported counts (12/0, 2/0, 6/0) are corroborated by my independent hand enumeration above but not by any included machine-generated log. If the parent expects reproducible executable evidence, this is a packaging gap.

Minor ambiguity: the e03-guidance counterexample '照搬设备可行解，把Q3的20人安排在C1-S3……20>12，非法' (exercise-data.json:422) is valid and realizable — mapping the E01 feasible solution R1->D1/S1, R2->D2/S2, R3->D1/S3, R4->D2/S3 would place Q3 at C1-S3 — but it does not arise from mapping the E01 reference solution, which puts R3 at D2-S2 (i.e., Q3->C2-S2, legal) and R4 at D1-S3 (i.e., Q4->C1-S3, which would instead be illegal on two grounds: 16>12 capacity and missing computers). A reader could assume the counterexample is the mapped reference; one clarifying line would remove the ambiguity, though the teaching point itself is correct.
questions: Is the empty executable-evidence.json (input_sha256 = SHA-256 of the empty string) intentional under the read-only/no-execution policy, or should a non-empty enumeration log accompany verification_script_sha256 before parent acceptance?

Should the e03-guidance counterexample note that it maps from a non-reference E01 feasible solution (R3->D1/S3), so readers do not assume the mapped E01 reference solution itself produces the illegal Q3->C1-S3 placement?
uncertainties: Solution counts (12/0 for E01, 2/0 for E03, 6/0 for E05) were re-derived by hand enumeration from the constraint and data files; the read-only role forbids executing the verification script, so script-level reproducibility of the reported counts is confirmed only by independent reasoning, not by running code.

The interpretation of evidence.json 'choices' arrays as per-request legal position sets (with the E01 duplicate entry corresponding to R3/R4 having identical option sets, flagged by duplicate_rejected) is inferred from the data and counts; the files do not document the schema of that field.
Whether executable-evidence.json hashing to the empty string is an intentional placeholder under the no-execution policy or a packaging omission cannot be determined from the provided files alone.
